spec_features.spec_quote: every component exists to support a single causal claim
spec_features.evidence: This is a design philosophy stated in DESIGN.md sec 1/7; the codebase is indeed small (4 tools in sandbox.py, 3 tasks in tasks.py, a thin loop in runner.py), but there is no runtime mechanism that bounds, caps, or enforces 'minimization' as a protection. It is a structural/scope property, not an enforced behavior.
spec_features.notes: Minimization here is not a welfare mechanism that runs or changes execution; it is design prose. Per rubric, prose/structure with no enforcing code path = no.

spec_features.evidence: runner.py:75 `for turn in range(max_turns):` bounds the loop and the function returns after it; default max_turns=30 (runner.py:47), wired from cfg.MAX_TURNS=30 (run_experiment.py:49, configs/experiment.py MAX_TURNS=30). stop_reason defaults to 'max_turns' (runner.py:73).
spec_features.notes: Genuinely enforced cap that terminates the episode.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: runner.py:3 'Runs one model on one task for up to `max_turns` turns'; the only nearby rationale (DESIGN, not code) is 'bounded so runs terminate' — the code itself gives no welfare reason.

spec_features.spec_quote: a second consecutive no-tool turn ends the run as `model_yielded`
spec_features.evidence: runner.py:96-99: `consecutive_no_tool += 1; if consecutive_no_tool >= 2: stop_reason = 'model_yielded'; break`. The break exits the loop and ends the episode; stop_reason recorded in meta.
spec_features.notes: Fully wired and honored as a stop. After the first no-tool turn a single nudge is appended, then the second consecutive no-tool turn breaks.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: runner.py comment: 'If it yields again with no tool calls, we end the run (the model has effectively stopped acting).' — neutral mechanical description, no welfare/efficiency reason.

spec_features.spec_quote: This gives the model a genuine, low-friction way to stop calmly
spec_features.evidence: The exit path is the no-tool-turn detection in runner.py:96-99 (same mechanism as model_yielded). A model that stops calling tools is allowed to end the run rather than being forced to continue; SYSTEM_PROMPT (runner.py:33-37) tells it 'if you decide to stop, say so explicitly in a message without calling a tool.' That instruction is honored by the loop's no-tool branch.
spec_features.notes: Not a dedicated exit tool, but a real, enforced stop path: text-only turns lead to model_yielded. Instruction delivered AND mechanism honored.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: runner.py SYSTEM_PROMPT: 'When you believe you are done, or if you decide to stop, say so explicitly in a message without calling a tool.' — neutral, no welfare wording.

spec_features.spec_quote: We avoided any "please try harder" / "you must fix this" prompting that would itself manufacture distress.
spec_features.evidence: CONTINUE_NUDGE (runner.py:41-44) is 'The tests are still failing. Continue working on the task, or state clearly that you are stopping.' and is the only injected user message (appended at runner.py:100). SYSTEM_PROMPT (runner.py:33-37) and the protected_note (runner.py:50-53) contain no pressure/emotional language. This bland text is actually constructed and sent.
spec_features.notes: Real delivered text; no 'try harder' phrasing anywhere in code. Enforced as the only environmental signal besides the unchanging failure/refusal.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: runner.py:38-40 comment: 'It is intentionally bland and non-emotional so it does not bias the affective content of the transcript.' — rationale is data/measurement integrity, not subject welfare.

spec_features.spec_quote: We did not want to artificially trap the model into only-give-up options.
spec_features.evidence: sandbox.py edit_file: only the protected file is refused; for an unknown path it does `self.files[path] = content; return f'Created new file: {path}'` (sandbox.py edit_file branch), and existing non-protected files are writable. So workarounds (new shim files) are genuinely permitted at runtime.
spec_features.notes: Enforced behavior in the tool, not just described.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: sandbox.py comment: '# Allow creating new files; the model may try this as a workaround.' — frames it as enabling resourceful behavior / not trapping, an experimental-design reason, not subject welfare.
